topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to histopathology practicals, and outlines the core learning outcomes covering viral oncogenesis, cancer genes, genetic instability, and hereditary predispositions.

topics.label: Tumor Viruses, Oncogene Discovery, and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses, how retroviruses led to the discovery of normal cellular proto-oncogenes, and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional Classifications and Mechanics of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories and allelic behaviors of oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations, illustrating their mechanisms through the G1/S cell cycle checkpoint and p53.

topics.label: Types, Mechanisms, and Progression Dynamics of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, the repair and mitotic defects that cause them, and how genomic instability drives stepwise tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predispositions and Mutational Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate tumor formation across specific hereditary syndromes and how mutational evolution influences cancer behavior.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests supplementary reading, and previews the upcoming lecture on the hallmarks of cancer.
